title: Client activation check-in (scratch)
content:
Context:
- Prep for weekly AE/CS 1:1 with Priya (AE on Client A) before the account health sync. Client A onboarding hit two slowdowns last week: SSO cert delay and initial inference latency spikes on their staging workload.
- Goal: align on mitigation status, decide if we put a temporary capacity uplift on Dedicated, confirm next customer-facing message, and capture owner + deadlines for blockers.

Quick metrics to cite (from dashboard):
- Ingestion success: 98% (goal 99.5%)
- Avg token latency (staging): 340ms p95 (target <= 200ms)
- Error rate (inference): 0.6% last 7d (baseline 0.1%)
- Signup -> activation time: 12 days (expected <5 for small customers)

Meeting agenda (20 min):
1) 3m recap of current state (what customer sees)
2) 5m technical root-cause & mitigation update (SSO cert, CI spikes)
3) 6m tradeoff discussion: temporary Dedicated uplift vs incremental optimization
4) 4m message & owner alignment for customer update + next checkin
5) 2m quick risks and escalation plan

Talking points / notes for me to mention:
- On latency: we saw KV cache thrashing on their long prompt distribution; we recommended prefix caching and a reduced batching window. Need confirmation if priya's eng contact pushed the client-side change.
- SSO: legal/ops cleared cert; deployment blocked by client infra team (ticket CORE-1423). Suggest offering a short call with our SRE to unblock.
- Costs: if we propose temporary Dedicated uplift, estimate incremental cost ~ $6k/week; position as temporary (2–3 weeks) while we land optimizations.

Questions to ask Priya (AE):
- Have they given the infra engineer permission to add our SRE to their deploy channel? If yes, which Slack handle?
- Did they try the reduced batching window patch on staging after Monday's deploy? Any measurable change?
- How sensitive is the business to the activation delay? Is there a hard launch date we must meet?

Proposed customer-facing message (short):
"Thanks again — we identified two blockers (SSO cert and cache behavior causing latency spikes). We're offering a quick joint runbook session with your infra engineer and our SRE to get SSO deployed, and as a contingency we can provision short-term Dedicated capacity to stabilize latency while we implement caching improvements. Planning to follow up with a proposed time for the runbook and an update in 48 hours."

Action items (capture in ticket/Slack after the call):
- Priya (AE): Confirm SRE contact / permission to join client deploy channel. Due: 2025-11-13.
- Sanjay (me): Open an internal SRE quick-ops thread and request availability; attach current latency traces and p95 plots. Post thread link to CORE-1423. Due: 2025-11-13.
- Amira (CS): Draft customer-facing note and share with Priya for sign-off. Due: 2025-11-14.
- Luis (solutions eng): Run a quick simulation of the reduced batching window on a mirrored dataset and share inferred p95 improvement estimates. Due: 2025-11-15.
- Product (optional escalation): Evaluate temporary Dedicated uplift pricing and capacity; standby if AE requests. Point person: Priya to escalate to sales ops. Due: 2025-11-14.

Potential escalation / guardrails:
- If staging p95 remains >300ms after caching change, recommend immediate 24–72h Dedicated uplift. Notify SRE lead and finance ops before provisioning.
- If SSO cannot be deployed within 48h, propose a scoped workaround (JWT test key for staging) — requires legal sign-off (low-risk dev key).

Notes to self (post-call prep & follow-ups):
- Bring p95 chart and the KV cache heatmap (last 72h) into the call screen share.
- Bring cost calc sheet (quick) for Dedicated uplift: baseline vs temporary.
- Make sure to capture verbatim client quotes on sensitivity to latency; this will drive escalation.

Rough script / warm open: 
"Quick order — want to align on blockers and a pragmatic plan. We can either stabilize quickly with temporary capacity while we deploy an optimization, or we can attempt a live optimization first if you're comfortable with a slightly longer window. Which approach would you prefer?"

Follow-up logging checklist (after meeting):
- Update CORE-1423 with agreed action items and owners (Sanjay).
- Post message to slack:#acct-client-a summarizing customer message (Amira).
- Create a short Confluence note: "Client A activation incident — timeline + remediation" (Sanjay/Amira) and link in ticket.

Freeform / scratch ideas (not for customer):
- Could we provide a low-cost transient buffering layer (micro-queue) to smooth bursts instead of full Dedicated? Engineering feasibility check with Luis.
- Consider waiving first week of Dedicated uplift if client contracts to 3 months reserved after activation (sales incentive). Pass to Priya for feedback.

Last-minute reminders:
- Keep the ask simple: just one meeting to unblock SSO and confirm whether uplift is needed.
- Avoid promising timelines >48–72h unless ops committed.

End of notes.
